source_text: ΙΓʹ. Κεφάλαιον δὲ τοῦ λόγου· Μετὰ τῶν χερουβὶμ δόξασον, συναγόντων τὰς τρεῖς ἁγιότητας εἰς μίαν κυριότητα, καὶ τοσοῦτον παραδεικνύντων τῆς πρώτης οὐσίας, ὅσον ὑπανοίγουσι τοῖς φιλοπόνοις αἱ πτέρυγες. Μετὰ Δαβὶδ φωτίσθητι, πρὸς τὸ φῶς λέγοντος· Ἐν τῷ φωτί σου ὀψόμεθα φῶς, οἷον ὥσπερ ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τὸν Υἱόν· οὗ τί ἂν γένοιτο τηλαυγέστερον; Μετὰ Ἰωάννου βρόντησον, τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς βροντῆς, μηδὲν περὶ Θεοῦ ταπεινὸν ἠχῶν, μηδ' ἀπὸ γῆς, ἀλλ' ὑψηλὸν καὶ μετέωρον (τὸν ἐν ἀρχῇ τε ὄντα, καὶ πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν ὄντα, καὶ Θεὸν Λόγον, Θεὸν γινώσκων, καὶ Θεὸν ἀληθινὸν ἐξ ἀληθινοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀλλ' οὐ σύνδουλον ἀγαθὸν, υἱοῦ προσηγορίᾳ μόνῃ τετιμημένον· καὶ τὸν ἄλλον Παράκλητον, δηλαδὴ ἄλλον τοῦ λέγοντος· Θεοῦ δὲ ὁ Λόγος)· καὶ ὅταν μὲν, Ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν, ἀναγινώσκῃς, τὸ συναφὲς τῆς οὐσίας ἐνοπτριζόμενος· ὅταν δὲ, Πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα, καὶ μονὴν παρ' αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα, τὸ διῃρημένον τῶν ὑποστάσεων λογιζόμενος· ὅταν δὲ, τὸ Πατρὸς, καὶ Υἱοῦ, καὶ ἁγίου Πνεύματος ὄνομα, τὰς τρεῖς ἰδιότητας. ΙΔʹ. Μετὰ Λουκᾶ ἐμπνεύσθητι, ταῖς Πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων προσομιλῶν. Τί μετὰ Ἀνανίου τάττῃ καὶ Σαπφείρας τῶν καινῶν νοσφιστῶν (εἴ γε καινὸν ὄντως ἡ τῶν ἰδίων κλοπὴ), καὶ ταῦτα νοσφιζόμενος, οὐκ ἀργύριον, οὐδ' ἄλλο τι τῶν εὐτελῶν καὶ μικρῶν, οἷον γλῶσσαν χρυσῆν, ἢ ψιλὴν, ἢ δίδραχμον, ὥς ποτε στρατιώτης ἄπληστος, ἀλλ' αὐτὴν κλέπτων θεότητα, καὶ ψευδόμενος, οὐκ ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ Θεὸν, ὅπερ ἤκουσας; Τί; Μηδὲ τὴν ἐξουσίαν αἰδῇ τοῦ Πνεύματος, ἐφ' οὓς θέλει, καὶ ἡνίκα, καὶ ὅσον πνέοντος; Ἐπιδημεῖ τοῖς περὶ Κορνήλιον πρὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος, ἄλλοις μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων. Ὥστε ἀμφοτέρωθεν, ἔκ τε ὧν ἐπιφοιτᾷ δεσποτικῶς, ἀλλ' οὐ δουλικῶς, καὶ ἐξ ὧν ἐπιζητεῖται πρὸς τὴν τελείωσιν, τὴν θεότητα μαρτυρεῖσθαι τοῦ Πνεύματος. ΙΕʹ. Μετὰ Παύλου θεολόγησον, τοῦ πρὸς τρίτον οὐρανὸν ἀναχθέντος· ποτὲ μὲν συναριθμοῦντος τὰς τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις, καὶ τοῦτο ἐνηλλαγμένως, οὐ τετηρημένως ταῖς τάξεσι, προαριθμοῦντος, ἐναριθμοῦν τος, ὑπαριθμοῦντος τὸ αὐτό. Ἵνα τί; Δηλώσῃ τὴν ἰσοτιμίαν τῆς φύσεως. Ποτὲ δὲ τῶν τριῶν μεμνημένου· ποτὲ δὲ τινῶν, ἢ τινὸς, ὡς ἑπομένου πάντως τοῦ λείποντος· καὶ ποτὲ μὲν τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Πνεύματι διδόντος, ὡς οὐδὲν διαφέροντος· ποτὲ δὲ, ἀντὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος, τὸν Χριστὸν ἐπιφέροντος· καὶ ὅτε μὲν διαιρεῖ τὰς ὑποστάσεις, εἷς Θεὸς, λέγοντος, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν· καὶ εἷς Κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς, δι' οὗ τὰ πάντα, καὶ ἡμεῖς δι' αὐτοῦ. Ὅτε δὲ συνάγει τὴν μίαν θεότητα· ὅτι ἐξ αὐτοῦ, καὶ δι' αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα, δηλαδὴ διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος, ὡς πολλαχοῦ δείκνυται τῆς Γραφῆς. Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Glorify the Trinity with witnesses of Scripture
orientation: Gregory closes the homily by urging his hearers to glorify the Trinity together with the cherubim, David, John, Luke and Paul, and to confess the full divinity of the Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: But the summing up of the speech is this. Glorify with the cherubim, who gather the three holinesses into one lordship, and who show forth of the first being as much as the wings open up to the earnest. Be enlightened with David, who says to the light: In your light we shall see light, as in the Spirit the Son; than which what could become more far shining. Thunder with John, the son of thunder, sounding nothing lowly about God, nor from earth, but high and lifted up, knowing him who both is in the beginning, and is toward God, and is God Word, God, and true God from true Father, but not a fellow slave who is good, honored by the name of son by title only; and the other Comforter, that is other than him who speaks; but the Word is of God; and whenever you read, I and the Father are one, beholding in a mirror the joined thing of the being; but whenever, We shall come to him, and we shall make a dwelling with him, reckoning the divided thing of the persons; but whenever, the name of Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, reckoning the three properties. Be inspired with Luke, conversing with the Acts of the apostles. Why do you rank yourself with Ananias and Sapphira, the new embezzlers, if indeed the theft of one's own things is truly new, and embezzling these things, not silver, nor any other thing of the cheap and small things, such as a tongue of gold, or a bare one, or a double drachma, as once a greedy soldier, but stealing divinity itself, and lying, not to man, but to God, which you heard. What. Do you not even feel shame before the authority of the Spirit, who blows upon whom he wills, and when, and as much as he wills. He visits those around Cornelius before the baptism, others after the baptism through the apostles. So that from both sides, both from the things to which he comes as master, but not as slave, and from the things for which he is sought toward completion, the divinity of the Spirit is witnessed. Theologize with Paul, who was taken up to the third heaven; at one time counting together the three persons, and this in exchanged order, not kept to the ranks, counting first, counting among, counting under the same thing. For what purpose. That he may show the equal honor of the nature. At another time remembering the three; at another time some, or one, as the missing one surely following along; and at one time giving the activity of God to the Spirit, as differing in nothing; at another time, instead of the Spirit, bringing in Christ; and when he divides the persons, saying, one God, from whom all things, and we to him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom all things, and we through him. But when he gathers together the one divinity: that from him, and through him, and to him are all things, that is through the Holy Spirit, as is shown in many places of Scripture. To him be the glory to the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: ἴδιος means one's own or private property, fitting Ananias and Sapphira keeping back their own price, which makes the paradox that Gregory calls new
rejected: theft of what belongs to God

choices.english: who blows upon whom he wills
choices.why: ἐφ᾽ οὓς is epi plus accusative plural of the relative, persons upon whom, not place where

pass_b_english: This is the sum of my argument. Glorify with the cherubim, who gather the three holinesses into one lordship and disclose only as much of the first being as their wings open to those who labor with love. Be enlightened with David, who speaks to the Light, "In your light we shall see light" (Psalm 36:9), as seeing the Son in the Spirit. What could shine brighter from afar than this?

Thunder with John, the son of thunder. Sound nothing low about God and nothing earthbound, but only what is high and lifted up. Know him who was in the beginning, and was with God, and was God, the Word (John 1:1), true God from the true Father, not a good fellow slave honored only with the title of Son. Know also the other Comforter (John 14:16), other, that is, than the one who speaks, for the Word belongs to God. When you read, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30), see mirrored there the union of being. When you read, "We will come to him and make our dwelling with him" (John 14:23), reckon there the distinction of the persons. When you read the name "of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19), see there the three particular properties.

Be inspired with Luke, and dwell with the Acts of the Apostles. Why do you rank yourself with Ananias and Sapphira, those new embezzlers — if theft of one's own things is truly new? You hold back no silver and no other cheap and small thing, no tongue of gold, no bar of silver, no double coin, as that greedy soldier once did, but you steal divinity itself. You lie, "not to men, but to God" (Acts 5:4), as you have heard. Why do you not even respect the authority of the Spirit, who blows upon whom he wills, and when he wills, and as much as he wills? He visits those with Cornelius before baptism, and others after baptism through the apostles. From both sides, then, the divinity of the Spirit stands attested: from those upon whom he comes as master and not as slave, and from those for whom he is sought for their completion.

Do theology with Paul, who was taken up to the third heaven. At times he counts the three persons together, and he does this with shifting order, not fixed by rank, putting the same one first, next, and last. Why? To declare the equal honor of their nature. At times he names all three, at times only some or one, since what is left out surely follows. At times he gives the activity of God to the Spirit, as making no difference. At times he brings in Christ instead of the Spirit. When he divides the persons, he says, "One God, from whom are all things, and we for him, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him" (1 Corinthians 8:6). When he gathers together the one divinity, he says, "For from him, and through him, and to him are all things" (Romans 11:36), that is, through the Holy Spirit, as Scripture shows in many places. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: You lie, "not to men, but to God" (Acts 5:4), as you have heard.
last_rejected.source_quote: ψευδόμενος, οὐκ ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ Θεόν, ὅπερ ἤκουσας
last_rejected.why: The quotation reads as the words he utters. Gregory means he lies to God, not to a human, as Scripture said.
last_rejected.fix: You lie not to men but to God (Acts 5:4), as you have heard.
last_rejected.ruling: The source ψευδόμενος, οὐκ ἄνθρωπον, ἀλλὰ Θεόν is itself Acts 5:4 verbatim, and Gregory's 'as you have heard' follows it. The English tracks that; the claimed ambiguity is minor.
